claims.content: The C2 JU wants to manage track identity classification by classifying track identity per the standard definitions, distinguishing exercise tracks from live operational tracks via the Exercise Indicator, resolving detected identity information differences, and determining when to assume or relinquish reporting responsibility (R²), so that only the JU with the best positional and velocity data reports the track on the interface.

scope_contract.goal_statement: The C2 JU wants to manage track identity classification by classifying track identity per the standard definitions, distinguishing exercise tracks from live operational tracks via the Exercise Indicator, resolving detected identity information differences, and determining when to assume or relinquish reporting responsibility (R²), so that only the JU with the best positional and velocity data reports the track on the interface.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: A C2 JU is managing a track identity classification for which an identity information difference or an R² determination condition has arisen; the JU resolves the difference via the appropriate J7 message and applies the R² determination, achieving a consistent track identity classification reported by the best-positioned JU.
scope_contract.start_boundary: The C2 JU is managing a track identity classification for which an identity information difference or an R² determination condition has arisen.
scope_contract.success_boundary: The C2 JU has resolved the detected identity information difference and determined the correct R² state, achieving a consistent track identity classification reported by the JU with the best positional and velocity data.
in_scope_actions: Classify track identity according to standard definitions (Pending, Unknown, Assumed Friend, Friend, Neutral, Suspect, Hostile)
Distinguish exercise tracks from live operational tracks using the Exercise Indicator
Resolve detected track identity information differences via appropriate J7 messages
Determine when to assume or relinquish reporting responsibility (R²)
variant_dimensions: Track identity category (Pending, Unknown, Assumed Friend, Friend, Neutral, Suspect, Hostile)
Exercise Indicator (exercise vs live operational track)
Identity information difference type (Identity, Special Interest Indicator, Exercise Indicator, Platform, Platform Activity, Environment/Category, IFF/SIF, Strength)
R² trigger message type (J7.0, Drop Track, J2 PPLI)
Resolution mechanism (manual vs J7 message transmission)

claims.content: C2 JU

The C2 JU is managing a track identity classification for which an identity information difference (Identity, Special Interest Indicator, Exercise Indicator, Platform, Platform Activity, Environment/Category, IFF/SIF, or Strength) or an R² determination condition has arisen.

The C2 JU has previously accepted the defined field values for Platform, Platform Activity, Specific Type, and Special Interest Indicator fields, and the system is configured to accept all defined field values for retransmission and operator appreciation when assuming R² for a previously-reported track.

The trigger for managing track identity classification is the detection of an identity information difference (Identity, Exercise Indicator, Platform, Platform Activity, Environment/Category) or the arising of an R² determination condition. Specifically, this includes detection of a mismatch between Local Data and Remote Data identity classifications, receipt of a track report with changes in Environment/Category, Identity, or Exercise Indicator (with PPLI Track Number and Identity Indicator set to value 1), assuming R² for a previously-reported track (unless the JU holds locally derived data other than No Statement (non-NS) that differs from the value accepted for retransmission), or operator initiation of a J7.5 Clear IFF/SIF (ACT=0) or IFF/SIF Update Request (ACT=2).

The C2 JU detects an identity information difference for the track (Identity, Special Interest Indicator, Exercise Indicator, Platform, Platform Activity, Environment/Category, IFF/SIF, or Strength), or an R² determination condition arises; the C2 JU then classifies the track identity according to the standard definitions: Pending, Unknown, Assumed Friend, Friend, Neutral, Suspect, or Hostile.

To distinguish exercise tracks from live operational tracks, the C2 JU sets the Exercise Indicator in the J3 track message; when the Exercise Indicator is set to value 1 (Exercise Track), the standard identity of the track is Friend and the exercise identity is specified in the Identity Amplifying Descriptor field.
The C2 JU detects an identity information difference for the track (Identity, Special Interest Indicator, Exercise Indicator, Platform, Platform Activity, Environment/Category, IFF/SIF, or Strength).
The C2 JU resolves the detected identity information difference by transmitting the appropriate J7 message.
The C2 JU receives a J7.0 (ACT=0) Drop Track message from the FJU on the locally held track.
Immediately prior to assuming R² for an air or surface track after receipt of the Drop Track message, the C2 JU tests the track for correlation, conducting the test only once.

The C2 JU assumes R² at the next opportunity to transmit the track because it has correlated local sensor data, local reporting eligibility remains, and a remote report has not been received on that track.

After assuming R², the C2 JU reports the IU as a track or point on the Surveillance Network PG by transmitting a J3.XC1 message, which triggers surveillance data reporting at the next opportunity; the surveillance message type depends on the Environment/Category of the IU, the Identity is reported as Friend, the Track Number, Platform and Platform Activity values received in previous PPLI messages are reported, and the PPLI Track Number and Identity Indicator is reported as value 1.

After assuming R², the C2 JU retains R² for the track until it is relinquished in accordance with the R² rules or until the track is dropped; it relinquishes R² for a real-time track upon reception of a remote track report in which remote TQ is greater than local TQ, or upon reception of a remote track report with TQ equal to the local TQ from a JU whose STN/Source TN is greater than the local STN/Source TN. When an Environment/Category change is made or a difference report is rejected, it reports the local Environment/Category in the appropriate Surveillance report if it has R², or in a J7.0 (ACT=1) message for conflicts if it does not; when an R² JU changes the Environment/Category, the decision to retain the original TN or report the entity with a new TN is made in accordance with paragraph 4.4.2.8 and Table 4.7-1. Upon receipt of a J7.0 (ACT=6) message, it automatically sets the Identity Amplifying Descriptor to Exercise Friend for tracks with the Exercise Indicator set to value 1.

Diverges from Step 4: When a track report with the PPLI Track Number and Identity Indicator set to value 1 contains changes in Environment/Category, Identity, or Exercise Indicator, the C2 JU may elect to accept those changes automatically, provided the new identity is Friend and the locally held identity is not Hostile.

Diverges from Step 5: The C2 JU assumes R² of an IU in accordance with real-time track reporting rules when it has correlated local sensor data and any of the following occurs: no J2 PPLI message has been received for 40–60 seconds; a J2 PPLI message (other than J2.0) is received with the NPS Indicator set to Inactive or Conditional Radio Silence; a J7.0 (ACT=0) Drop Track message is received from the FJU for a PU, RU, or other IU; or the Geodetic Position Quality in a J2 PPLI message is set to value 0.

Diverges from Step 5: If the C2 JU receives a J2 PPLI message with the NPS Indicator set to TDS Failure from a JU that has R² of a locally held track, it may assume R² at the next opportunity to transmit the track if local reporting eligibility remains and a remote report has not been received on that track.

Diverges from Step 5: If the C2 JU does not receive a J7.0 (ACT=0) Drop Track message and receives no further updates on a remote track, it may automatically purge the track (DRT=0–3) after a system-selected time interval, which should consider the irregular reporting of subsurface surveillance tracks.

Diverges from Step 6: If the correlation test finds a track for which another C2 JU has R² and the Track Numbers are the same, the C2 JU accepts the PPLI information into its surveillance database and disregards the J3 surveillance data on that track; if the Geodetic Position Quality in the PPLI message is set to value 0, it instead accepts the surveillance track and discards the PPLI message.

Diverges from Step 6: If the correlation test finds a track for which another C2 JU has R² and the Track Numbers are different, the C2 JU transmits the J7.2 Correlation message with RV=1, using the Source TN in the Header word of the J2 PPLI message as the Retained TN and the surveillance TN as the Dropped TN.

Diverges from Step 6: If the correlation test finds a track for which the C2 JU itself has R², it transmits the J7.2 Correlation message with RV=1 using the Source TN in the Header word of the J2 PPLI message as the Retained TN and the surveillance TN as the Dropped TN, ceases reporting the track, and transmits a J7.0 (ACT=0) Drop Track message on the surveillance TN.

Diverges from Step 6: If position or other data in the J2 PPLI meet decorrelation criteria, the C2 JU decorrelates the PPLI and local track data, initiates a new surveillance track report with locally held data using a new track number, and reports both the PPLI Track Number/Identity Indicator field and the PPLI IFF/SIF Indicator field as No Statement.
Diverges from Step 7: For a nonreal-time track with the TQ field set to value 0, a C2 JU without R² assumes R² for that track when the track is locally updated by a new nonreal-time report.

Diverges from Step 8: When the C2 JU assumes R² for a previously-reported track, it retransmits values accepted for retransmission unless it holds locally derived data other than No Statement that differs from the accepted value; in that case, it reports the locally derived data instead.

missing_aspects: The claim's specific enumeration of 'Platform, Platform Activity, or Specific Type fields' is not fully supported by EC-AF-041, which refers generally to 'the field'. While EC-AF-012 mentions these fields, it describes them as an exception to the general rule rather than defining the scope of the primary condition. The rewritten claim removes the unsupported list to remain strictly faithful to the general rule defined in EC-AF-041.

claims.content: Diverges from Step 3: If the local data and the received data differ as to whether the TN is assigned to a point or to a track, the operator shall be alerted.

Diverges from Step 4: When Local Data is PENDING and Remote Data is HOSTILE (or vice versa), the system response is '1*' OPERATOR ALERT, requiring the operator to take a manual action to accept or reject the received ID.

Diverges from Step 4: In the PENDING-HOSTILE, UNKNOWN-HOSTILE, and SUSPECT-HOSTILE cases, systems MAY have a feature to automatically accept the received ID as local ID, overriding the default manual alert requirement.

Diverges from Step 4: When an operator receives an IFF/SIF data conflict alert, the following manual actions are available for attempting resolution: update local data manually or verify automatic inputs; initiate J7.5 (ACT=0) Clear IFF/SIF message (any mode); initiate J7.5 (ACT=1) IFF/SIF Difference Report message (any mode); change local data to agree with remote data except in the case of Mode II code; decorrelate the local data from the remote data, causing the assignment of a new track number to local data; or clear operator alert (any mode).

Diverges from Step 4: For J7.5 (ACT=1) Difference Reports transmitted by non-R² JUs, the system transmits to report a difference in accordance with Table 4.7-5 IFF/SIF Difference Resolution Matrix; this transmission may be initiated by operator action anytime.

Diverges from Step 4: When a JU changes the Environment/Category of a track as specified in the list (e.g., Space to air, Air to surface) or when a difference report is rejected by an operator action, the information shall be reported: if the JU has R², the local Environment/Category shall be transmitted in the appropriate Surveillance report; if the JU does not have R², the local information shall be transmitted in the J7.0 (ACT=1) message for conflicts.

Diverges from Step 4: During resolution of differences for Platform/Platform Activity/Specific Type fields, the C2 JU shall retain received values for retransmission and operator appreciation, except when (a) a value of 0 (No Statement) is received while a non-zero value is held locally; or (b) an Air Platform value of 6 (Tanker), 7 (Tanker Boom Only), or 8 (Tanker Drogue Only) is held locally and a different value is received.

Diverges from Step 5: There may be cases when a system does not receive a J7.0 (ACT=0) message and receives no further updates on the remote track; in that case, each system will have the capability to automatically purge those tracks (DRT = 0-3) after a system-selected time interval, and shall not transmit a J7.0 (ACT=0) message on the purged remote track.

Diverges from Step 5: If the C2 JU receives a J2 PPLI message with the NPS Indicator set to Inactive, Conditional Radio Silence, or TDS Failure from a JU that has R² of a locally held track, it may assume R² at the next opportunity to transmit the track if local reporting eligibility remains and a remote report has not been received on that track.

Diverges from Step 6: If a correlation is found with a track for which another C2 JU has R² and the TNs are the same, the JU receiving the J2 shall accept the PPLI information into its surveillance database and shall disregard the J3 surveillance data on the specified track; however, when the Geodetic Position Quality in the PPLI message is set to value 0, the surveillance track is accepted and the PPLI message is discarded.

Diverges from Step 6: If a correlation is found with a track for which another C2 JU has R² and the Track Numbers are different, the J7.2 (RV=1) Correlation message shall be transmitted, with the Source TN as the Retained TN and the surveillance TN as the Dropped TN.

Diverges from Step 7: If the JU has not received a remote report on a locally held Air or Surface (Maritime) track for approximately 40 seconds, or on a locally held Land (Ground) track for approximately 120 seconds, it assumes R².

Diverges from Step 8: As an explicit exception to the local data override rule, non-NS data for Platform, Platform Activity, and Specific Type fields received from the controlling unit for the track are retransmitted regardless of locally derived data.

Diverges from Step 8: Data updating can occur spontaneously as a result of the R² unit reporting a No Data status (value 0) for one or more modes in a required IFF/SIF Surveillance data report, J3.XC1.

Upon successful resolution of an identity information difference (e.g., Identity, Exercise Indicator, Platform, Platform Activity, or Environment/Category), the appropriate J7 message (e.g., J7.5 ACT=1 Difference Report or J7.5 ACT=2 Update Request) has been transmitted, and the track identity classification reported by the best-positioned JU (R² unit) is consistent across the network.

After an Environment/Category change or operator rejection of a difference report, the local Environment/Category has been reported in the appropriate Surveillance report if the JU had R², or in a J7.0 (ACT=1) message for conflicts if it did not have R²; when the R² JU made the change, the original Track Number was retained or a new Track Number was assigned in accordance with Table 4.7-1.
Upon receipt of a J7.0 (ACT=6) message, all JUs automatically set the Identity Amplifying Descriptor to Exercise Friend for tracks with the Exercise Indicator set to value 1.

After applying the rules for assuming or relinquishing reporting responsibility (R²), R² is retained by the JU until it is relinquished in accordance with those rules or until the track is dropped; after correlation and resolution of duplicate information, duplicative information is not transmitted on the Surveillance Network PG.

After assuming R² of an IU, the C2 JU reports the IU as a track or point on the Surveillance Network PG with Identity reported as Friend, Track Number, Platform and Platform Activity values from previous PPLI messages retained, and the PPLI Track Number and Identity Indicator set to value 1 (maintained if another C2 JU assumes R²); a J3.XC1 message has been transmitted at the next opportunity, initiating periodic surveillance data reporting.

After successful completion of the surveillance reporting process, R² units report all IFF/SIF valid data locally held for a track in accordance with J3 message transmit rules, while non-R² JUs monitor such data and report it only if they hold different data via a J7.5 message.

quality_flags.detail: [mainflow_trigger_continuity] The Trigger enumerates the identity information difference types as "Identity, Exercise Indicator, Platform, Platform Activity, Environment/Category", but Preconditions and Main Flow step 1 require the full set "Identity, Special Interest Indicator, Exercise Indicator, Platform, Platform Activity, Environment/Category, IFF/SIF, or Strength". Special Interest Indicator and Strength are absent from the Trigger (and IFF/SIF appears only as an operator-initiated J7.5 action), so the Main Flow cannot be started for those difference types.

[mainflow_trigger_continuity] The Trigger explicitly includes operator initiation of a J7.5 Clear IFF/SIF (ACT=0) or IFF/SIF Update Request (ACT=2) as a triggering event, but Main Flow step 1 restarts with only "detects an identity information difference ... or an R² determination condition arises". There is no step or branch that receives and processes the operator-initiated J7.5 Clear/Update Request, so this trigger path is not continued.

inconsistency_hints: Precondition claim 0 states that an identity information difference or R2 determination condition has already arisen before the use case begins. The trigger claim, however, says the trigger is the detection of the identity difference or the arising of the R2 determination condition. If the condition has already arisen as a required precondition, its arising cannot still be the initiating event. The trigger should be the subsequent detection/recognition of that already-arisen state, or the precondition must not assert the condition as already present.

The main flow does not lead to several declared postconditions. It has no step for the Environment/Category reporting and Table 4.7-1 track-number handling required by postcondition 2, no receipt/processing of J7.0 (ACT=6) to set Identity Amplifying Descriptor to Exercise Friend required by postcondition 3, and no R2 relinquishment handling to support postcondition 4's rule that R2 is retained only until relinquished or dropped. Thus the main flow is incomplete as a path to the stated final outcomes.

The goal explicitly requires determining when to assume or relinquish reporting responsibility (R²), but the provided main_flow claims (steps 1-8) only cover the assume-R² path. No main_flow claim addresses R² relinquishment, so the goal is not consistent with the complete behavior described in main_flow.

Exception flow claim 8 only states that there may be cases when a system does not receive a J7.0 (ACT=0) Drop Track message and receives no further updates on the remote track. It gives no outcome: no return to main_flow, no termination/handoff, and no explicit terminal failure/prevention state. The branch is incomplete.

The Trigger says the use case is initiated by detection of an identity information difference, by the arising of an R² determination condition, or by operator initiation of a J7.5 IFF/SIF action. Main Flow step 1 instead starts with generic track-identity classification, and the triggering detection is not reached until step 3 (with the R² assumption event in steps 5-7). Step 1 is therefore not a continuation of the Trigger; the flow restarts as a classification scenario and re-derives the trigger later.

After successful completion of the surveillance reporting process, R² units report all IFF/SIF valid data locally held for a track in accordance with J3 message transmit rules, while non-R² JUs monitor such data and report it only if they hold different data via a J7.5 message.
